BMW's M2 Grows Muscles in All the Right Places, Albeit Only Digitally
10 photos
Photo: Instagram | rotislav_prokop
While its larger sibling, the BMW 3 Series , has already tapped into the Neue Klasse era, with the range-topping M3 joining it perhaps a few months to roughly one year from now, the 2 Series Coupe will live on for a few more years in its current form.
The second-generation entered production at San Luis Potosi in Mexico in the second half of 2021, and a little over two years ago, it was replaced by the LCI (Life Cycle Impulse), which is Bimmer slang for facelift. The 2er Coupe shouldn’t be confused with the 2 Series Gran Coupe, because it is based on the CLAR (Linie Klein) platform, just like the old 3 Series, 5 Series, 6 Series, X3, X4, Z4, and others, including the M2.
The Gran Coupe on the other hand shares nothing but the 2 Series name with the two-door model, because it is based on the same platform as the F70 1 Series, as well as the 2 Series Active Tourer, the X1, X2, MINI Countryman, and others. All of these rides utilize the front-biased UKL2 construction, whereas the 2er Coupe is a rear-biased machine, just like the larger 3 Series, 4 Series, and so on.
And since we mentioned the M2 two paragraphs above, we should remind you that the second-generation is only three years old, and was joined by an xDrive all-wheel drive variant earlier this year. Launched for the 2027 model year, it is called the M2 M xDrive Coupe, and boasts the same amount of power as its rear-wheel drive sibling.
Photo: Instagram | rotislav_prokop This means 473 horsepower (480 ps/353 kW ) at 6,250 rpm and 443 pound-feet (600 Nm) of torque from 2,700 to 5,620 rpm, which makes it a bit less punchy than the M2 CS . The latter has 523 hp (530 ps/390 kW) and 479 lb-ft (650 Nm) of torque to play with, and can hit 60 mph (97 kph) in just 3.7 seconds. That’s actually one-tenth of a second slower than the M2 M xDrive Coupe, whereas the RWD M2 Coupe will reach 60 mph in 4.1 seconds.
BMW’s M2 CS starts at $98,600 in the United States of America, so it is one pricey cookie. The M2 M xDrive Coupe has an MSRP of $73,600, according to the company’s official local website, whereas the regular M2 Coupe, aka the rear-wheel drive one, kicks off at $69,500. The M240i xDrive Coupe and the M240i Coupe start at $55,600 and $53,600, and have 386 hp (391 ps/288 kW) on tap, taking 4.1 and 4.4 seconds from 0 to 60 mph (97 kph), respectively.
Now, given that the second-gen BMW M2 has been around for three years, we have seen quite a few tuning takes on it. However, one of the latest to have crossed our screens is also on the fake side of things. Why is that, you ask? Because the tuning fairy is actually a rendering fairy in this case, as the pictured project came from @rotislav_prokop on social media.
The CGI artist rearranged the pixels of this machine in order to make it look a lot more appealing, and before inviting you to leave your impression in the comments box at the bottom of the story, we should delve into some of the things that make this car stand out. These include the extremely wide front fenders and rear three-quarter panels, which make it look like it belongs at the racetrack and not on public roads.
Photo: Instagram | rotislav_prokop Up front, it has been virtually altered with a modified bumper, as well as a fat apron, and there are side skirt extensions on deck, too, as well as a modified rear bumper that is significantly wider than before, a new diffuser with a motorsport-like extra brake light in the middle, and a ducktail spoiler.
The wheels are extremely wide, and they have also come from the CGI-infused aftermarket world, and the car features a lime green paint finish on the outside, and several black elements, as well as what seems to be a carbon fiber roof. If the latter is indeed on deck, then this virtually-modded BMW M2 Coupe has a lower center of gravity, so it corners faster. The alloys, with their wide lips and visible rivets, mix a silver and black finish, and the suspension has also been tuned.
According to the rendering artist behind these digital illustrations, this BMW M2 is said to have a “ more elegant attitude, ” and “ the goal ” was to make it “ wider, more distinctive, and more sophisticated, while keeping the character that makes the M2 so special. ” I definitely dig the makeover, and I think that this thing would have been a lot cooler if it featured a racing-inspired livery. But hey, I’m not going to complain about it, as I like the project, as mentioned above. But do you? And would you see yourself behind the wheel?
